data.long_meaning: The one who preserves, protects, memorizes and keeps the Quran in memory. The name Hafza carries the meaning “Preserver, Memorizer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, English. Parents who choose Hafza usually hope their child will grow to embody preserver, memorizer and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Hafza
in_english.long_meaning: Hafza means preserving and remembering: This name is derived from the Arabic root 'hafiza', which means to preserve and remember. In Islamic tradition, hafiza is considered a blessed name, as it is associated with the qualities of remembering and preserving the divine revelation. The name Hafza is also associated with the concept of memory and remembrance, which are essential for a Muslim's spiritual growth and development. This name is considered auspicious, as it is believed to bring blessings and protection to the bearer.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hafsa is of Arabic origin and is derived from the verb "hafaza", which means "to preserve, protect, safeguard, keep, or memorize". Historically, women in Islamic society who were known for their memorization and recitation of the Quran were often given the title of "Hafsa" or "Hafizah". These women were respected not only for their academic achievements but also for their piety and dedication to the preservation of the Divine Word. The name Hafsa thus carries a profound sense of intellectual and religious achievement that is deeply rooted in Islamic tradition and culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic theology, the Quran is considered the living Word of God and the ultimate source of guidance for mankind. Memorizing the Quran is considered a highly meritorious act, as it enables one to continually engage with and reflect upon the Divine Message. Hafsa, as a name, signifies a deep connection to the Quran and a commitment to its preservation, both in the heart and mind. It is a reminder of the spiritual importance of memorization and recitation, and a testament to the belief that the Quran is not just a historical text, but a living, transformative force in the lives of believers.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Preserver, Memorizer" symbolizes The one who preserves, protects, memorizes and keeps the Quran in memory.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Hafza serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of preserver, memorizer.
